paper_title: Cooling of young neutron stars and dark gauge bosons
coupling_convention: e' = U(1)_{B-L} gauge coupling g_BL, dimensionless, exactly as plotted on the y-axis
notes: Paper constrains both dark photons and U(1)_B-L gauge bosons from cooling of young neutron stars (Cas A, NS1987A). Per the VectorBL hint, extracted the B-L bound: conservative limit e' < 5e-13 (Eq. 40), explicitly stated to be mass-independent for m_gamma' < Tc(n3P2) = O(0.1) MeV = 1e5 eV, since the B-L coupling to neutrons is not plasma-suppressed. Encoded as a flat bound; lower mass edge of 1e-6 eV is not explicitly stated by the paper (the bound formally extends to m->0; Fig. 7 shows the exclusion region but numerical values are not tabulated), which is the main uncertainty. A stronger bound e' < 1e-13 applies only if envelope parameter eta < 1e-11; the conservative eta-independent value 5e-13 is used. Paper also reports dark photon bounds eps*m < 1.5e-8 MeV (Cas A) and 3e-9 MeV (NS1987A), not extracted here. No formal confidence level stated (astrophysical cooling argument); 0.95 is nominal.
